targets.title: The effects of making public service employees aware of their prosocial and societal impact: a microintervention.
targets.evidence_quote: To address concerns about the generalizability of findings to the population of public employees, this article brings V&W2020 "into the wild" by conducting a replication of their study set among a sample of real-world Danish caseworkers.
targets.outcome_quote:
This study brought the theoretical underpinnings from V&W2020 "into the wild," testing if making a sample of real-world public employees aware of their prosocial or societal impact yielded similar effects as when conducted among MTurkers. Our main result is that scholars should be cautious about expecting interventions tested on MTurkers to work as well in a real-world setting.
None of the experimental intervention groups in our study differed much from the control group; neither in terms of turnover intention nor job satisfaction.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors contrast the original benefits with no intervention/control differences in the replication; limitations do not declare this attempt incapable of adjudication.
